title: Add HierarchyNode_tenantId_sowId_idx via a plain CREATE INDEX migration

approvals.evidence: "Approve the migration (Recommended)" -- AskUserQuestion, 2026-09-06. prisma/schema.prisma and prisma/migrations/ are protected paths; this is the required explicit approval before implementation.

body.design_ref: None -- the index mirrors the composite tenantId-first pattern HierarchyNode's other two indexes (parentId, deletedAt) already use.

steps.title: Add @@index([tenantId, sowId]) to HierarchyNode in prisma/schema.prisma; validate with npx prisma validate.

Hand-author the migration (this session has no shadow database, so prisma migrate dev cannot generate it): a single CREATE INDEX "HierarchyNode_tenantId_sowId_idx" ON "HierarchyNode"("tenantId", "sowId") -- not CONCURRENTLY, since this repository's migrations run inside prisma migrate deploy's own per-file transaction (CONCURRENTLY cannot) and this codebase has no precedent for a non-transactional migration.

Apply the migration to the configured database via npx prisma migrate deploy, run directly from this session rather than through .github/workflows/deploy.yml -- a deliberate exception, justified by: the user's explicit approval already covering "the live-database proofs"; the migration being purely additive with zero interaction with any code the deploy pipeline's ordering rules protect (nothing currently deployed changes what it reads/writes because this index exists); and this session already running the same category of direct-database verification (audit:persistence, audit:rls, audit:integrity) throughout. Recorded explicitly in the validation result rather than left implicit.
steps.verify_command: npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma generate

steps.title: Confirm the index exists via a direct pg_indexes query, then run the full verification suite plus all three live-database proofs.
steps.verify_command: npx tsc --noEmit && npm run audit:tenancy && npm run audit:attribution && npm run audit:contracts && npm run validate:scenarios && npm run audit:persistence && npm run audit:rls && npm run audit:integrity

commit_boundaries: All four steps as one commit: one schema change, one migration, applied and proven together.
body.rollback: The index can be dropped (DROP INDEX "HierarchyNode_tenantId_sowId_idx") without any data loss or application-code change, since nothing reads or writes differently because it exists -- it only changes a query plan. Reverting the commit reverts the schema.prisma declaration and leaves the already-applied migration file in git history; a genuine rollback of the applied database state would additionally need the DROP statement run by hand, since prisma migrate deploy has no built-in down-migration.
